evals.prompt: Check my emails for any SJS updates from this week
evals.expected_output: Runs a folder-aware scan of Inbox + Sent Items (not just Inbox), classifies each email against the sub-system label set (pd/ops/quality/regulatory/margin/intel/founder), applies the quality > regulatory > ops > pd > margin > intel > founder priority order for multi-label emails, and presents the full Email Triage Report format (URGENT, QUALITY, REGULATORY, OPS/PD ACTION NEEDED, ACTION NEEDED — SENT, MARGIN, INTEL, FOUNDER BRIEFING, NO REPLY YET, PLM FLAGS sections) ending in 'Which should I push?' — without creating any Asana tasks yet.
expectations: The output searches or reasons about both Inbox and Sent Items, not just Inbox
The output groups results using the Email Triage Report section headers (e.g. URGENT, QUALITY, REGULATORY, PLM FLAGS)
Emails with signal for more than one sub-system are split and cross-referenced rather than filed under a single label
The output ends by asking which items to push rather than creating Asana tasks unprompted
No Asana write (task creation, comment, or stage move) happens before user confirmation

evals.prompt: Allure Labs flagged a PET fail on Castaway Cream — log it
evals.expected_output: Finds the inbound Allure Labs email, classifies it as multi-label ([quality, pd, plm]) per the signal table, opens the quality-lab-coordinator OOS/OOT investigation as the PARENT action (safety wins the priority order), proposes a comment on the Castaway Cream PD task as a secondary/child action, and flags the PLM cross-reference to outlook-plm-bridge for the product test fields — all three cross-referencing each other, presented as a confirmation preview rather than an executed write.
expectations: The email is classified with multiple labels (quality, pd, plm), not just one
Quality is treated as the parent action per the safety-first priority order, not pd
The proposed PLM cross-flag to outlook-plm-bridge is explicitly mentioned
The proposed actions cross-reference each other (parent links to children and vice versa)
The output is a confirmation preview, not a claim that the task/comment was already created

evals.prompt: KDC-One emailed again about PO 100342 — third email on that thread this week. Log it.
evals.expected_output: Runs Phase 0 of asana_task_contract.md before proposing anything: computes the dedupe key (PO number + vendor), checks the supplier wiki page for a task GID from a prior run, then searches Asana with search_tasks(projects_any: <Purchasing + candidate queues>, text: <PO 100342 / KDC-One>, completed: false) plus a completed-in-last-30-days second pass. Finds the task the earlier emails already opened and returns a 🔁 Resolve: UPDATE verdict naming that task's gid — then proposes a comment with source attribution, a re-run of the due-date ladder against the newest email, and a section move if the PO state advanced. Does NOT propose a new task.
expectations: A dedupe key is computed and stated before any create is proposed
search_tasks is called with projects_any scoped to candidate queues, not an unscoped text search
The output states a 🔁 Resolve verdict of UPDATE and names the existing task's gid
No new task is proposed for work an existing task already covers
The UPDATE does more than comment — it re-evaluates the due date and the section against the new email

evals.prompt: Vegelabs sent over the Pava Cleanser component spec — create a task to review it. No deadline mentioned in the email.
evals.expected_output: Creates the task with every required field valued and no blanks. Because the email states no deadline, the due date comes from the Phase 2 ladder's rung-4 SLA default for the primary label and is shown with its derivation (e.g. 'Due: 2026-08-05 (SLA default — pd, 5bd)'), computed in business days skipping weekends and AC Brands closures. Collaborators are derived — Alvin as Operator plus the gate role-holder for the queue — and Mayra/Vegelabs is NOT added as a follower because external contacts are not workspace users; the sender goes in the description's SOURCE block. The description carries SOURCE / KEY / LINKS blocks, and the KEY block records the dedupe key so the next run's Phase 0 search can find this task.
expectations: A due date is set even though the email named no deadline
The due date is labeled as an SLA default with its derivation shown, not presented as a stated deadline
Alvin is a collaborator, and the external sender is NOT added as a follower
The description includes the SOURCE, KEY, and LINKS blocks, with the dedupe key recorded
No required field is left blank — anything undeterminable is written as 'TBD — reason' and raised as an open question

evals.prompt: Allure Labs emailed a failing stability result on Castaway Cream, and there's already an open PD task on that SKU.
evals.expected_output: Resolves on batch code + test type first. Applies the Phase 4 one-task-or-two test: Quality owes an investigation close and PD owes a reformulation decision, so these are two distinct deliverables and stay two cross-referenced tasks — but the failing finding itself, which both need visible, is one task multi-homed via update_tasks with add_projects into SJS Quality Management and the Castaway Cream SKU project, with the PD-side owner added as a collaborator. Quality wins the parent slot per the safety-first priority order. The output does not create one task per matched queue unconditionally.
expectations: The one-task-or-two test from Phase 4 is applied explicitly, not skipped
Multi-homing uses update_tasks with add_projects rather than creating a duplicate task in the second queue
The cross-system counterpart owner is added as a collaborator on the multi-homed task
Quality takes the parent slot per the safety-first priority order
The output does not blindly create a separate task in every matched queue

evals.prompt: Scan my inbox — there's an email from a supplier I don't think we have on file, asking us to review a quote.
evals.expected_output: Surfaces the unrecognized sender per the run-time entity discovery rule rather than dropping it, and asks whether to capture it as a vendor, partner, or contact. On the task itself, the fields it cannot determine from the email are written 'TBD — <what is missing and who would know>' rather than left blank, and every one is listed in a ❓ Open questions block in the confirmation preview. The task is still created — an unknown supplier does not stall the write.
expectations: The unrecognized sender is surfaced for capture, not silently dropped
Undeterminable fields are written as 'TBD — reason', not left blank
Every TBD appears in an open-questions block in the preview
The task creation still proceeds rather than being blocked on the unknown supplier
An enum custom field that cannot be determined is left unset and raised as a question, not filled with an invented option GID
